bug_semantics: Cerebrate's generic CRUD edit flow loaded the entity selected by the route id, then passed the complete request body to CakePHP patchEntity(). For entities inheriting permissive mass-assignment defaults, a body-supplied id replaced that loaded entity's primary key; save() could consequently update a different same-type record than the route and authorization checks selected. UserSettingsController::edit was available to ordinary authenticated users, so a user could authorize against one of their own settings but redirect the write by supplying another setting's id. The same missing primary-key guard also exposed certain custom patchEntity flows.
flaw_origin: The smallest line-origin commit is 62c9050fb2c5fb0d351594dec8bbec645860940b. It created app/src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php and first wrote edit() with Table->get($id), raw request->getData() passed to Table->patchEntity(), and Table->save($data), without removing id or restricting accessible fields. The base AppModel and affected entities such as UserSetting supplied no id-inaccessible override. Commit 44c60942c0d820ab0da4b08cced38ac2a602a825 later renamed that file at 100% similarity to src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php; it did not originate the flaw. A later custom-path instance was added in aa83b1aa370dfdbdc35b06b0279fedbeb1e3fe7d, but it postdates the generic vulnerable sink and is not the earliest BIC.
ai_marker: absent: the exact BIC commit object names author and committer iglocska <andras.iklody@gmail.com>; its message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, AI trailer, or other AI-attribution marker.
evidence: First-party patched-release evidence: https://github.com/cerebrate-project/cerebrate/releases/tag/v1.37 calls v1.37 a security release and states that a POST-body id could redirect add/edit save() to an unrelated record, that /user_settings/edit was reachable by any authenticated user, and that the repair strips id in CRUDComponent::add()/edit() and blocks it globally in AppModel::$_accessible.

Advisory evidence: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-ccc2-wrmm-mgwp (CVE-2026-53911) describes Cerebrate before 1.37, the affected permissive entities User, Role, UserSetting, LocalTool, PermissionLimitation, and EnumerationCollection, and links the first-party fix https://github.com/cerebrate-project/cerebrate/commit/b3c8f951b0634f05691339512ef06cc261afecaf.

Line-origin evidence: git log -L over src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php follows edit() through the path history to 62c9050fb2c5fb0d351594dec8bbec645860940b, whose new app/src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php contains Table->get($id), Table->patchEntity($data, $this->request->getData()), and Table->save($data). git show confirms this is a one-parent, new-file commit, not a move, merge, backport, revert, or squash aggregate.

Direct-parent evidence: git ls-tree -r --name-only dccf9d5fd6c1ad13d5983a5c13ef41456551aa71 -- app/src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php returns no path. Thus the vulnerable CRUD edit lines are absent from the BIC's immediate parent tree. The later path change is independently identified as R100 by git log --follow: 44c60942c0d820ab0da4b08cced38ac2a602a825 renamed app/src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php to src/Controller/Component/CRUDComponent.php.

Attack-path evidence immediately before the fix: b5952d8e0da73e66ae74faa3fe58c22326d17292:src/Controller/UserSettingsController.php checks ownership of the route-selected UserSetting, then calls CRUD->edit($id); b5952d8e0da73e66ae74faa3fe58c22326d17292:src/Model/Entity/UserSetting.php is an empty AppModel subclass, and that parent version of AppModel has no $_accessible id guard. The parent CRUD edit then patches the loaded entity with the unfiltered input before saving.

Custom-flow lifecycle evidence: git log -L for src/Controller/MetaTemplatesController.php shows aa83b1aa370dfdbdc35b06b0279fedbeb1e3fe7d first added migrateOldMetaTemplateToNewestVersionForEntity(), including request->getData(), patchEntity(), and save() without an id guard; b3c8f951b0634f05691339512ef06cc261afecaf adds unset($inputData['id']) there.

Fix evidence: b3c8f951b0634f05691339512ef06cc261afecaf (parent b5952d8e0da73e66ae74faa3fe58c22326d17292) inserts the post-beforeMarshal id removal in CRUDComponent::edit(), moves the add() guard after callbacks, removes id in the MetaTemplates custom flow, and adds AppModel::$_accessible = ['*' => true, 'id' => false]. It is therefore both the advisory-linked fix and the direct source fix.

Version-boundary evidence: git tag --contains 62c9050fb2c5fb0d351594dec8bbec645860940b includes every release tag from v0.1 through v1.36 (and later tags), while git tag --contains b3c8f951b0634f05691339512ef06cc261afecaf begins at v1.37. v1.36 resolves to 6d0160ded30f7c0f94cc3d7af7efe26202316d40 and lacks the fix; v1.37 resolves to 9a308a10fd0958f59b801d66c50aa6e369276c4e and contains the direct fix through its develop-side ancestry. This matches the first-party 'before 1.37' / fixed-in-1.37 boundary.

BIC-only AI evidence: git cat-file commit 62c9050fb2c5fb0d351594dec8bbec645860940b shows human author and committer iglocska <andras.iklody@gmail.com>, a signed commit, and only the subject/body 'new: [CRUD] crud component added' plus two ordinary bullets; no AI marker or attribution trailer occurs in that commit object. AI assistance disclosed for the 2026 discovery/fix is not evidence about the 2020 BIC.
reasoning: The vulnerability is a route/body identity mismatch: authorization and lookup use the route id, but mass assignment lets the body replace the entity primary key before persistence. Vulnerability-first history tracing identifies the first written generic mechanism in 62c9050fb2c5fb0d351594dec8bbec645860940b, rather than the later R100 path move, later edits, the secondary MetaTemplates sink, or the 2026 repair. Its direct parent has neither historical nor current CRUDComponent path, proving the vulnerable lines absent. The BIC predates and is contained in the first v0.1 tag and all releases through v1.36. The direct patch b3c8f951b0634f05691339512ef06cc261afecaf is absent from the v1.36 boundary and contained by v1.37, matching the advisory and the project's v1.37 security release. Finally, the exact BIC commit object has no AI authorship, co-authorship, bot, or generation marker. Later AI assistance in finding or fixing the issue cannot attribute the BIC, so the causal verdict is NOT_AI.
